extracted.intended_audience: unagented fiction writers preparing unsolicited submissions to Tor / Tom Doherty Associates (Tor & Forge)
extracted.subtask_short: submitting unsolicited fiction to Tor & Forge
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for unagented authors preparing and mailing unsolicited fiction proposals (science fiction, fantasy, general fiction, children's/YA) to Tom Doherty Associates (Tor & Forge). Covers required packet contents, manuscript formatting, addressing, and postal/response policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript sample — first three chapters or 40–60 pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submissions packet should include the first three chapters of your book prepared in standard manuscript format on white paper. If your chapters are really short or really long, or you don't use chapter breaks, you may send the first 40-60 pages of your book, provided you stay under 10,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted text must be made up of consecutive pages and should end at the end of a paragraph, not in mid-sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard manuscript format (page-level formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must be prepared in standard manuscript format on white paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard manuscript format means margins of at least 1 inch all the way around; indented paragraphs; double-spaced text; and Courier or Times Roman in 10 or 12 pitch. Use one side of the page only and do not justify the text. Do not bind the manuscript in any way. Make sure the header of the ms. includes either your name or the title of the book and the page number (on every page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis of the entire book
rubrics_metrics.description: A synopsis of the entire book must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The synopsis should include all important plot elements, especially the end of the story, as well as aspects of character development for your main characters. The synopsis should run between three and ten pages in standard manuscript format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dated cover letter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a dated cover letter with your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter must include your name and contact information and the title of the submitted work. Briefly tell which genre or subgenre the submission falls into and mention any qualifications you have that pertain to the work. Please list any previous publications in paying markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-addressed stamped, business-size envelope (SASE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a self-addressed, stamped, business-size envelope for the publisher's reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not include an SASE, you will not receive a reply at all. If you live outside the United States, consult USPS online postage options. Note: because of postal policy changes, the company may be unable to return submissions; they recycle proposals—so include an SASE to get a reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: One proposal per submissions packet
rubrics_metrics.description: Send only one proposal in each submissions packet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have written a series, send a proposal for the first book only. If they like what they see, they'll ask for the rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send a query letter instead of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send a query letter; the publisher prefers to see the proposal itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's practically impossible to judge a project from a query. They'd rather see your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: No email or fax submissions or status inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send submissions or inquiries by email or fax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They do not respond to emailed or faxed submissions, queries, or inquiries about the status of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No disks or electronic media
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send disks; the publisher wants printed pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They want to read words in black type on white paper. Also, submitted disks might carry computer viruses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send the only copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send your only copy of any material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items can get lost in transit; always keep a copy for yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send interior/cover art or author photo
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include interior or cover artwork or an author photograph with initial submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There will be time for art or photos later if the project is of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send gifts or three-dimensional items
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send jewelry, food, toys, 3-dimensional representations, or anything that might be construed as a bribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples they've received: handmade bracelets and earrings, anatomical models, home-baked cookies, fine fabrics, fancy bookmarks, coconuts, fancy manuscript boxes. Such items have no impact on consideration; the work must 'sink or swim on its own merits.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Address submissions by genre to the correct acquisitions editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Address submissions to the appropriate acquisitions editor according to genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing examples: Paranormal Romance: 'Acquisitions Editor, Paranormal Romance'; Science fiction and fantasy: 'Acquisitions Editor, Science Fiction and Fantasy'; General fiction (mysteries, thrillers, mainstream, women's fiction, horror): 'Acquisitions Editor, Fiction'; Children's and Young Adult: 'Acquisitions Editor, Children's and Young Adult Division'. Note: they publish chapter book, middle grade, and young adult audiences but do not publish picture books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and status policy
rubrics_metrics.description: General timeline and how to follow up (or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They generally respond to unsolicited submissions within 4-6 months. Because of volume and transit issues, they cannot track down individual projects; do not call for a status report. If you have not heard back after six months, please resubmit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission handling and recycling policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on returning unsolicited submissions and why returns may not be possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to postal service policy changes requiring heavier packages to be mailed at a post office and because the company uses a mailroom, they can no longer return submissions reliably. When they try, submissions are sent back to them or disappear in transit. They recycle your proposals (recycle = recycle white paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to request delivery confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want assurance that your manuscript was delivered, request postal delivery confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for a return receipt or a signature confirmation when you post it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postcard notifications are not useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Including a postcard to be returned upon receipt is unlikely to be helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They don't open submissions until they're ready to read them, so you'll likely get the 'I got it' postcard the same day you receive their response to your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission review workload and response style
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about how submissions are reviewed and the typical reply format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They have an open submissions policy and consider tens of thousands of projects a year. Every proposal that reaches them is reviewed by at least one member of the editorial staff. Because of volume, they primarily reply with form letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting continuity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted pages must be consecutive and end at paragraph breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the sample ends at the end of a paragraph, not mid-sentence, and that pages are consecutive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-count ceiling when sending sample pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If sending 40-60 pages because chapter breaks are irregular, the sample must still stay under 10,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets an absolute upper bound on the mailed sample when using the page-based allowance.
